title: Regression plan
description: The regression artifact the regression-impact-assessor writes for one Task: the impact scope before Red (plan mode) and the final mapping of the approved scope after Red (finalize mode). task-to-deploy.js accepts it against this file; scripts/portfolio/regression.py check, validate and verify it and run its runs. In finalize mode components, discovery, requirements and sourceFiles stay exactly as approved; only mappings, replacements and runs change.

sourceFiles.description: The absolute path of each regular file actually read to establish the scope, vault document backing files included; never a directory, a worktree or a repository root. Section citations go in the sourceRef fields. regression.py checks each is an existing regular file and binds its bytes when the scope is approved.

sourceRefs.description: The documents and sections searched, each a real document and requirement or section.

priorRequirementsSearched.description: True only when the sources the scope rule of skills/cumulative-regression/SKILL.md reaches (earlier PRDs, and the components and consumers it names) were actually searched; that rule bounds the search.

greenfield.description: True only with evidence that the component has no prior valid obligations; a missing ledger is not that evidence.

evidence.description: What the search found, and every missing or inaccessible source as an explicit gap.

requirements.description: Every current requirement the changed components carry: each still-valid prior requirement, and each this change can affect.

id.description: Source-qualified, so equal local IDs in different PRDs cannot collide; unique in the plan.

sourceRef.description: The document and the requirement or section that states it.

repoPath.description: The repository whose runs prove it; a run mapped to it has the same repoPath.

impacted.description: True when this change can affect it; an unaffected retained requirement is false, and its runs do not execute.

impactReason.description: The evidence for impacted, either way.

applicability.description: Exactly one entry for each of the four layers.

required.description: Whether the requirement needs evidence at this layer. A required layer of an impacted requirement needs a mapping to a run before verification.

reason.description: Why the layer is required or excluded, from the sources.

supersedes.description: Prior requirements this one replaces. Each needs an explicit accepted requirement or owner decision that authorizes the replacement; a new test, a changed implementation or a failing old test never does.

sourceRef.description: The accepted source that authorizes it.

mappings.description: Which run proves which layer of which requirement. In plan mode a mapping may be left out for tests still to be written; after Red every required layer of every impacted requirement has one. A mapping to a junit run names the tests whose assertions cover the requirement; a mapping to an exitStatus run is for the nonfunctional layer and names no tests.

runId.description: The id of a run in runs, in the requirement's repository.

testIds.description: For a junit run, the exact classname::name IDs its report emits, each one passing in it; empty for an exitStatus run.

replacements.description: A legitimate rename or consolidation of a prior mapped test, with equivalent assertion coverage. Distinct from requirement supersession.

reason.description: Why the new tests assert what the old one did.

runs.description: The commands the verification gate executes, each the repository's own supported command, run with /bin/sh in repoPath after its setup. A run executes only when an impacted requirement is mapped to it.

repoPath.description: The absolute path of the repository (or its worktree) the command runs in.

command.description: The command, never narrowed to a subset of the suite it gates.

format.description: junit: a test run that writes a fresh JUnit XML report to reportPath; the gate requires exit 0 and every mapped test ID passing in the report. exitStatus: a check whose whole result is its exit status, such as a lint, format or type check (for example the repository's ruff or mypy command); exit 0 passes the nonfunctional layer of each requirement mapped to it.

reportPath.description: For a junit run only: the XML report the command writes, under the repository's .agent-workforce/reports/, relative to repoPath or absolute.

setup.description: The preconditions of the run, in order: each a command the gate runs with /bin/sh in repoPath before the run, such as installing the repository's dependencies (for example `task install`). A setup command that exits non-zero fails the run with its output. A command shared by several runs of one repository runs once. Empty when the run needs nothing prepared.

reason.description: What the run needs from it, and what it needs to succeed (environment variables, credentials), from the repository's own instructions.

Layer.description: The test layer: unit, contract, integration, or nonfunctional (performance, resilience, security, and the repository's lint, format and type checks).
